d: A tactile writing system using raised dots arranged in 6-dot cells. Each cell stands for a letter, number or symbol, read by touch.
A visual language using handshapes, movement, facial expression and space. Sign languages differ between countries and communities.
Ask before helping, speak directly to the person, never touch a cane or guide dog, and face a person who lip-reads.
Use clear language, offer written and spoken options, describe visuals aloud, and allow extra time.
Missing captions, unlabeled signs, fast speech, and inaccessible forms can shut people out of everyday services.
Learn basic signs, organise awareness events, make notes accessible, and speak up for inclusive campus design.
Add alt text to images, caption videos, keep good colour contrast, and label buttons clearly.
